questions.question: What causes an aircraft to stall?
questions.explanation: A stall occurs when the wing exceeds its critical angle of attack, disrupting airflow and causing loss of lift.
steps: Recognize the question is about stalls.
Recall: stall = critical angle of attack exceeded.
Eliminate answers not related to angle of attack.
questions.fastStrategy: Stall = too high angle of attack, not speed.

questions.question: What is P-factor?
questions.explanation: P-factor is the asymmetric thrust produced by a propeller at high angles of attack, causing the aircraft to yaw.
steps: Identify P-factor as a propeller effect.
Recall: high angle of attack = more thrust on descending blade.

questions.question: What is the coffin corner?

choices.A: Where stall speed meets max speed

questions.explanation: Coffin corner is the altitude where stall speed and maximum speed converge, limiting the flight envelope.
steps: Recognize the term refers to high-altitude flight.
Recall: coffin corner = stall and max speed meet.
questions.fastStrategy: Coffin corner = stall speed meets max speed.
